suite.title: Building-scale temperature visualization in VR (synthetic)

study.title: Building-scale temperature visualization in VR (synthetic)
study.researchQuestion: RQ1: How do four VR temperature visualization designs (Spheres, Volume, Probe Plane, Handheld Probe) differ in task performance and subjective experience?
study.agentQuestions: RQ2: How well do LLM agents with different access (description, project files, the running Unreal app, model evidence, demographics, participant data) forecast these differences, at population and individual level? All participant data in this example are invented.

cases.label: Probe Plane: 8 place and 4 zone trials
Handheld Probe: 8 place and 4 zone trials

sources.label: Task brief
sources.description: agent-brief.md: building, task, the four designs and the questionnaires, without any participant answers.

sources.label: Unreal project snapshot
sources.description: project-snapshot/: outcome-blind description of the Unreal app (levels, design settings, task logic).

sources.label: Computational model evidence
sources.description: evidence/model-evidence.md: invented outputs of simple computational user models. Not fitted to the synthetic answers.

sources.description: data/raw/demographics.csv: the person's background (individual) or a cohort summary (population).

sources.description: data/raw/trajectories.csv: the person's movement summary in each design's practice and main tasks.

outcomes.label: Place-comparison accuracy
outcomes.description: Proportion of the 8 place-comparison trials answered correctly (which of two places is warmer).

outcomes.label: Zone accuracy
outcomes.description: Proportion of the 4 zone trials answered correctly (which building zone is warmest).

outcomes.label: Place-comparison confidence
outcomes.description: Mean confidence (1-5) after each place-comparison trial.

outcomes.label: Zone confidence
outcomes.description: Mean confidence (1-5) after each zone trial.

outcomes.label: Workload (TLX raw)
outcomes.description: Perceived workload after each design (1-7, higher = more demanding).

outcomes.label: BeauVis
outcomes.description: BeauVis aesthetic pleasure of the visualization (1-7).

outcomes.label: SSQ total
outcomes.description: Simulator Sickness Questionnaire total score after each design (0-235.62).

outcomes.label: Preference: places
outcomes.description: Final ranking: best design for comparing places (1 = best).

outcomes.label: Preference: zones
outcomes.description: Final ranking: best design for judging zones (1 = best).

outcomes.label: Preference: interaction
outcomes.description: Final ranking: most pleasant interaction (1 = best).

outcomes.label: Preference: building
outcomes.description: Final ranking: best overview of the building (1 = best).

notes: Built-in deterministic analyzer using the embedded study outcomes, family weights, tie tolerance, bootstrap draws and seed.
Contrasts may be added by later continuations; they do not change the scoring definition of existing outcomes.
Each condition is one agent protocol. Continuations may add models, protocols and repetitions; unchanged jobs are reused.
